reviewScope: Manual Arabic–English comparative review of 1,574 punctuation-delimited clauses in 75 units: original matn QT001–050 and 25 selected Tamhīd commentary units. Remaining 3,946 not individually certified.
sourceBasis: Current repository JS matn/commentary modules, retained edition N introduction and edition A main/conclusion
method: Source clause numbers are computed from Arabic punctuation. English ranges are manually matched, not proportional autoalignment. All segments in these eleven sections must be covered exactly once; unresolved readings remain explicit.

groups.note: Correctly gives the ancestor's completed objectives before introducing the closing problem.
The insufficiency of a brief treatise and the short indication are not conflated.
Instrumental science, discrimination between sound and unsound reasoning, and grounds of truth/falsity retained.
The opponent's assertion about spiritual wayfarers is stated as an apparent problem, not authorial verdict.
The apparent advantage of rational inquiry is reported as an inference to be addressed.
The experience-as-necessary-knowledge objection is retained. The base قانون يتبين الطريق حصولها is syntactically unstable.
Reply makes universal shared certainty a necessary condition; not all private experiences qualify.
Experienced contradictions and mutual denial are retained without denying all unveiling.
The weaker traveller's conviction and halt are attributed to a difference in preparedness.
The stronger traveller criticizes confinement to an attained object, not the object as such.
Concessive فرض التسليم and counterfactual instrument of discrimination are retained.
English now retains distinguishing some contents from others. Final Arabic البعض/النقص apparatus remains unresolved.
Purification and acquisition of theoretical knowledge are sequentially coupled, not made alternatives.
يصيرى and الغير المنسقة المنتظمة remain transcription cruxes. English is an expressly provisional construction.
Acquired malaka, certainty discrimination, and musical/metre analogies preserved.
الملوك is a problematic base form; travelling reads conjecturally as السلوك, without manuscript confirmation.
The malaka helps acquire and justify knowledge, and final comparative perfection is not omitted.
أقفاله/إقباله/أفعاله variants materially affect metaphor; the principal displayed reading is followed.
With a perfected guide present, station, time, preparedness, sciences and measures are individually related.
Length of further investigations and inadequacy of this concise commentary retained.
Author's devotional ending distinguished from the later editor's colophon.
Attribute/subject and necessary/possible are kept as incompatible predications of indistinguishables.
The possibility of graded predication is voiced in the opponent's objection, not decided as settled.
Accidental/essential (عارضة/ذاتية) and species-level predication (قولاً نوعياً) corrected; earlier extrinsic/intrinsic and 'specific manner' blurred the logical claim.
Fourfold dilemma, a-fortiori necessity and final denial of an entailing particular nature preserved.
Conceptual principles, essence-names, attributes, acts and relational names retained in order.
Assertoric principles are judgments of thubūt, not external physical existence.
Self-evident or higher-science principles and objection of the highest science retained.
First answer preserves effects, sense, reason, ḥads and kashf as distinguishable modes.
Second answer preserves reception from a more consummate unveiling as an analogue of higher science.
The objection requires a criterion and rejects merely imitative reception.
Double-negation reply denies that a discriminating measure is absent; person/time specificity retained.
Selective disclosure and the contrast of divine communication with satanic suggestion retained.
Domains of divine names are specified before the separate question of tawqīf.
The term tawqīfiyya is explicitly preserved as authoritative fixity; previous act-of-disclosure paraphrase exceeded the immediate wording.
Properties and special relations are included in the initial exposition; English reorders within the opening sentence.
Question in science requires demonstration in the relevant technical sense.
Demonstration as ordering certain principles to a judgment, and its analogue in this science, retained.
Two distinct argumentative responses identified: premise-denial and positive counterargument.
Necessity of unrestricted existence and ensuing multiplicity objection retained.
Counterclaim of external identity and reply based on independent existence distinguished.
The sanad as support for a denial is refuted only insofar as it is coextensive with the denial.
Priority, intensity, and perfection introduce the rival proof; inferential circularity is explained.
عرضية means accidental inherence, not mere extrinsicity; change of accidents' individuals or species is distinguished.
The al-Ṭūsī passage is a quotation within Tamhīd; not separately manuscript-collated.
Concessive reasoning, individuation, and historical celestial/elemental corporeality retained.
Opening sweeping objection remains attributed to the opponent.
Intelligible instances and possibility/necessity dilemma correctly ordered.
Unity of a specific nature and its essential entailments retained.
لو لم يقتض is inconsistent with the inferential role; displayed فلو اقتضى alternative remains source-disputed.
Second horn separates equivocity and necessary qualification of possible instances.
Reply restricts objection to determinate Necessary; به عين حقيقته remains a syntactic crux.
Unrestricted comprehensive existence contrasted with a determinate nature.
Challenge about possible entities and possibility in the Necessary preserved.
Crucial split: unconditional negation of possibility rejected; possibility of existence qua existence denied.
Polemical conclusion and Qurʾān 24:40 preserved.
Polemical description of disputants remains the author's, not the translator's.
Absence of added qualification sets up the objection about intrinsic necessity.
Reductio on necessity as an allegedly added restriction retained.
External qualifiers distinguished from necessary intrinsic judgments.
Intellectual considerations do not become extramental determiners.
Objection about all distinct concepts retained.
Response derives predication from intrinsic source rather than foreign determination.
Divine and cosmic names distinguished.
Bare self-evidence denial rejected as merely dialectical.
Four alternatives for particular existence are enumerated in order.
First (bare subject) versus second (accident alone) distinguished.
Third (composite of parts) rejected without smuggling in a modern ontology.
Objection limited to external impossibility answered.
Fourth (subject under accidental qualification) and intrinsic/relative unity preserved.
Possibility as manifestation of knowledge and necessity as manifestation of existence distinguished.
Closure objects to independently diverse existential instances.
Mental existence objection to equal modal status stated as opponent's.
Intelligible form's status as external accident contrasted with being-in-mind.
ما تكوّنت فيها and عند ملاحظته لما are problematic readings; translation provisional.
Unity in intrinsic being and diversity of consideration maintained.
Names/fixed entities and sequence spirits–imaginal–sensible retained.
Priority in reality versus final manifestation kept distinct.
بالفرض versus بالعرض remains an alternative at the final lemma.
Excluded merely conceptual sense and self-subsisting Necessary retained.
Introductory tanbīh and its supposed self-evidence reported; displayed ابيّة remains a lexical source crux.
Particular Necessary as wholly unlike its effects is set beside its shared general and existential predicates.
The argument is a purported inconsistency between absolute dissimilarity, causality, priority and shared universals.
Objection limits commonality to accidental and intellectual predicates; relation versus extramental affinity preserved.
Reply rejects genuinely distinct existential instances but retains relational differences.
The closing invitation to reflect is linked to the two foregoing replies.
First argument: intrinsic comprehensiveness and contrast of gathering/distinction; al-Ṣādiq maxim is attributed in source, not independently authenticated.
Objection to rhetorical 'more fitting' is retained.
Author's irony/rhetorical purpose preserved despite source's uncertain التغيير reading.
Light/color analogy preserves partial perceptual report and source's difficult ophthalmic metaphor.
First Arabic poem and concession to standpoint-dependent manifestation retained.
Closing elliptical verse has no explicit predicate; English marks [am] rather than falsely completing it.
Genuine unity and the notion of the first designation are attributed to Ibn Turka.
Multiplicity belongs to levels and names, not to unrestricted identity itself.
No real name or definition applies in the unqualified register; the terms are explained through conceptual consideration.
Name arising through negation is not a real name; descriptive definition via properties is excluded.
The apparent self-reference reductio and response by negative/non-real determination are distinguished.
Difference between non-real and real name-producing considerations retained without making determinations new substances.
Intellect's ability to abstract its own act and the gathering-of-opposites analogy remain, with unresolved تضايق/تعانق variants.

First tajallī is construed as a relation of knowledge; attributes are identical with essence under one determination yet accompanying under another. The English preserves this relativity rather than asserting an unqualified identity.
Arabic poetic quotation أنا أنت / أنت نحن / نحن هو and the encompassing presence are retained; original punctuation creates several short verse fragments.
Distinguishes essential from nominal perfection, most holy effusion and istijlāʾ; the fourfold division is an explicit exhaustive claim.
The first main division is according to the manifest (ẓāhir), requiring a wholly comprehensive Perfect Human locus, not an abstract genus.
Two subcases of manifestation from the manifest side: universality and particulars; Qurʾān 8:17 and Moses's speaking tree are retained as scriptural examples.
The second division is according to manifestation loci and subdivides self-manifestation of each individual and relational manifestation to another.
The final 'collectively and individually' excerpt is preserved; punctuation-splitting treats its printed ellipsis as four candidates, not four actual grammatical propositions.
The objection hinges on intellect/known as correlative opposites and alleges two existentially separate subjects; it is not Ibn Turka's endorsed conclusion.
The first reply is expressly dialectical, reducing the rival premise by appeal to self-knowledge of the Necessary and immaterial angels.
The dialectical reply is judged insufficient; the second answer distinguishes notional opposition from real existential distinction and uses iʿtibār as determining consideration.
Quiddities qua distinct are determining relations, in a register where no other exists outside absolute being. Labīd's quoted hemistich is distinguished from an independent prophetic utterance.
Degrees of appearance differ in clarity relative to our cognitive faculties, explicitly not as differences intrinsic to the undetermined reality.
Light and colored-glass analogy: colors belong to the mediating glass, not to light intrinsically. This is the commentator's analogy rather than an optical experiment.
The electronic Arabic للزجاج بدا شعاعة is syntactically disturbed; English 'radiance appears through the glass' is contextual, not a manuscript-established emendation.
No extramental distinction is asserted specifically 'at this level' for the quiddities insofar as distinct, not a categorical denial of worldly differences.
Identity in external being under a specified respect is distinguished from relative considered existence; the closing relation is not converted into an independent substance.
Closing injunction to reflect and prayer correctly attributed to the author.
Initial exclusion of the second case and meaning of the Necessary's determination being itself are retained.
Self-distinction is not differentiation through a separately added external quality; the dependence reductio follows.
Mere external thisness is rejected as the Necessary's essence because such an aggregate of relational accidents does not intellect itself or others.
Self-determination gives the Necessary what individual thisness gives a particular without identifying God with a heap of accidents.
Two-horned objection—non-exhaustiveness of fourfold division or common predication—is fully retained as adversary's objection.
Reply disambiguates shared meaning from commonality opposed to self-distinction and denies a separate counterpart.
Two kinds of determination—opposition versus comprehensiveness—distinguished by positive contradictory attributes versus a feature lacking in the other.
Marks of opposition are extrinsic relations; marks of comprehensiveness are intrinsic to being the whole/general, as an analogy not identification of the Necessary with a physical aggregate.
Comprehensive form's unity of gathering and Qurʾān 112:3–4 retained; the terse two positive opposition-kinds are not overexplained.
Concluding recurrence of individuality analogy and exhortation is present.
Undifferentiated first determination gathers aḥadiyya and wāḥidiyya; no real difference of names is being asserted at that initial register.
Hidden levels and letters still unarticulated within breath preserve the causal analogy; there is no premature physical creation claim.
Manifestation is predicated through its relations and affairs, expressly not the unconditioned essence qua essence.
Movement of love, volitional inclination and a second disclosure translated with source's syntactic variants around بحسبه تجلى noted.
Two grounds for calling it the Breath of the All-Merciful distinguished: formal articulation and relief of distress.
Ibn ʿArabī's quote reproduced as a quotation within the grandson's commentary; not an independently collated entire source.
All eight couplets retained; ellipses and uncertain images remain literal or bracketed, not rewritten as modern paraphrase.
Final author's explanatory remark and imperative to reflect are distinguished from the preceding Ibn ʿArabī verse.

Opening differentiates names by proper domain and levels; tawqīfī now retained as authoritatively fixed, not a distinct act of disclosure. Technical vocabulary used as controlled correspondence with reflective investigators.

One intrinsic unrestricted unity distinguished from relational numerical unity; the electronic Arabic duplicates one unit about unrestricted identity and the whole—not a different doctrinal proposition.
Aḥad and wāḥid distinguished as absence/affirmation of relations under considerations; numerical one illustrates naming, without a real duality in absolute essence.
First determination via encompassing rather than opposition, Muḥammadan Reality, four names علم/وجود/نور/شهود, and order of wordplay ẓuhūr/wijdān/iẓhār/ḥuḍūr preserved.
Essential perfection and perfection of the names are distinct by reference to hiddenness and manifestation, not two separate divine essences.
Existence and knowledge differ relationally in their objects at the manifest side, not by a separated essential subject.
Objection from the Peripatetic terminology of cognitive ḥuṣūl and causation retained; reply states equivalence of intended meaning after technical clarification.

A long distinct quotation from the ancestor's al-Ḥikma al-Rashīdiyya, with conditional alternatives about efficient influence and contact as an accident in a subject, preserved as quotation; no full independent source collation is claimed.
Strength of linkage varies with efficacy/mediating instruments; final الفرضية versus العرضية variant materially changes 'suppositional' versus 'accidental' conjunction.
Conclusion concerns lineage of sages as Ibn Turka's historical attribution, not established genealogical history; quotations of Hermes/Idrīs and Agathodaimon/Shīth are kept as attributed claims.

Order in self-knowledge is contrasted with a Peripatetic account whose effects are understood as existentially other; the critique is attributed to Ibn Turka and not treated as exhaustive Avicennan doctrine.
Seeming inconsistency between knowing entities and denying their separate existence is dissolved by two different considerations—intelligibility and created/caused otherness.
Two kinds of mental presence, receptive impression and active knowledge, are distinguished; possible printed المعقولية / المعلولية variant remains noted without conjectural emendation.

Attributed experiential account distinguishes knower-known identity from relational differentiation and withholds a further necessary concomitant; quotation is not identified as definitely by a particular author.

The closing argument has الفرضي / العرضي alternatives determining whether 'suppositional' or 'accidental' existence carries the dependence. English marks the base reading and variant rather than resolving it.

Conclusion distinguishes quiddities insofar as other—nonexistent—from quiddities without such otherness, which bear the intrinsic Necessary's real existence; the specific target of the making/causation critique is not broadened.
Opening الحمد لله رب العالمين is explicitly editorial adopted from catalogue incipit, not the A commentary's الحمد لوليّه; no codex collation claimed.

The subject is the difficult account of tawḥīd as the gnostics go to it and realized scholars indicate; disputants and reflective investigators distinguished without imposing commentator's identities on matn.
Opponents' old humoral diagnosis of bodily substrates, burning of healthy materials and black bile is reported, not endorsed as modern science.
Certainty in invalidation of rational/sensory/innate/natural judgments follows arbitrary asceticism as an opponent's causal claim; subsequent बीमारी is the adversary's diagnosis.
The adversarial objection is reversed, and the ellipsis marks a printed interruption before QT-004, not a conjectured restored authorial clause.
Aradtu to aradnā person change remains; ḥads is intellectual intuition, and the aim is proof in dialectical form rather than mere personal witnessing.
Author's prayer for salvation and avoidance of error retained.
Exhortation to seekers to acquire perfection and enduring life before necessary passing and natural death is complete.
Seek help and rely on God under the conditional believer qualification retained.
Existence common by meaning, not by word alone, kept distinct from the later stronger thesis of a numerically one external existent.
Proof uses contradiction of existence/nonexistence, not simply the assertion that existence is necessary; printed masculine لا يقبل after feminine حقيقته noted.
Necessity follows only after intrinsic impossibility of nonexistence; that inferential step is preserved.
Unrestricted Necessary is neither a concept qualified by generality nor privatively delimited.
Positive specifying qualifier is tested as form (composition) or accident (would not be intrinsic; otherwise no specification).
Dependence reductio and regress concern terms ordered between two present bounds, not an absolute mathematical denial of every infinity.
The objection is preserved. Malzūmāt is syntactically and philosophically difficult, and the English remains provisional until comparison with the separate ancestral manuscripts.
Later Peripatetic objection is reconstructed; māhiyya without conditioning by existence and extramental/mental distinction are kept within its dialectical role.
The claim of gradational predication of one existence upon particular existences is the opponent's position, not the ancestor's settled conclusion.
The double-existence charge and the distinction between the nature and what is shared in existence kept as opponent's reply.
External sameness and intellectually additional predication preserved under different considerations.
If necessary nature had mental individuals, some could exist and others be impossible; the author infers possibility per se for the class.
Modality per aliud versus per se and final axiom that what is intrinsic cannot be removed externally preserved.
First two reasons: determination identical with the reality, or necessarily required by the reality itself.
Third: intrinsic determination makes the nature unintelligible as one among many possible subjects.
Fourth: no association with another; intellectual or mental plurality thereby excluded.
Distinct real quiddity versus extramental existence produces mere verbal homonymy, not shared meaning.
Alternative non-distinction forces either denial of shared predicates or making possible instances bear necessary reality.
No intrinsic possible aspect or receptivity belongs to what is claimed necessary through itself.
Similars without a differentiating reason cannot be assigned mutually incompatible roles of accident inhering and subject as locus.
Dual-stage refutation: existential reality refuses both existence and nonexistence, hence intrinsically necessary; plurality would follow from a second intrinsically necessary existent.
Priority, perfection, intensity and completeness are introduced as an opponent's proposed ground; proving the entity thereby is circular.
Nature and determinate qualification distinguished, including external/mental subjects and privative/positive accidents.
Hypothesis that necessary nature is the underlying subject of absolute determination by gradation or equivocation remains an objection.
Reply preserves one intelligible concept of determination, varying with relational subjects; knowledge of the relation does not imply comprehension of the relata's intrinsic nature.
Intrinsic determination distinguished from an externally added predicate and mere individual thisness; unusual Arabic gender agreement preserved.
Necessary's self-distinction is analogous to individuality without equating Necessary with it.
Necessary as knower, known and intellect in itself, with three terms preserved.
Relational intelligibility to every intellect distinguished from exhaustive comprehension of its essential reality.
Association is excluded only if the other is an incompatible opposite; not every mode of relation is denied.
Two directions/modes of association between the Necessary and considered relations preserved.
Opposing speaker applies fourfold dilemma against unrestricted existence; existential plurality of mental instances is made hypothetical.
Second horn is equivocation versus necessitation of contingent instances, not an unconditional affirmation of either.
Printed conclusion به عين حقيقة and ملزومه retain textual/grammatical strain; the English follows commentary as provisional rather than establishing a manuscript reading.
The objection that intrinsic necessity restricts unrestricted reality is quoted as an objection, and the reply distinguishes necessary judgments from additional external qualifications.
No extramental restriction arises merely from a necessary predicate; the absolute/qualified distinction remains intact.
The pedagogical objection argues that answering a refuted hypothesis wastes proof and gives adversaries unnecessary openings; both claims retained.
The comparison between objective being and common quiddities grounds a distinction for the intuitive thinker, not simply a dismissal of opponents as unintelligent.
Difficulties of common imaginative assumptions and the benefit of rebutting doubts in training seekers preserved.
A controversial claim of self-evidence is rejected in the context of the dispute.
First two alternatives: bearer with no accident versus accident without existence considered.
Third alternative: aggregate of accident and subject; its supposed external impossibility is argued.
Fourth alternative: qualified bearer; the intrinsic/accidental distinction does not become a plurality of essential existents.
Alleged incompatibility is denied by appeal to the earlier proof.
Mental existence used in objection; reply asserts intrinsic identity of mental and external being under different considerations.
بالفرض / بالعرض would change suppositional to incidental predication, and the translation explicitly follows the displayed electronic base.
First principle as a specific species-like entity is argued incompatible with both complete external unrelatedness and subsumption under common predicates.
The admonition appeals to insight/intellect/discernment rather than asserting established manuscript history.
Final كون عينيّ تكون طبيعته عن تلك الأكوان is syntactically unstable; English reports a contextual unity rather than an independently attested emendation.
More fitting and more necessary maintains the author's graded rhetorical assertion while distinguishing absolute objective being and considered determinations.
No real names/qualities are predicated of the unrestricted essence in this particular consideration.
Negative predication as a notional determination is distinguished from adding a genuine external qualification.
Exhortation to contemplate follows the attributed argument.
First knowledge relation is self-presence of the unrestricted identity, not a representation of external objects.
Four consequences (necessity, necessitation, effusion, and other attributes) are not conflated into independent divine substances.
Knowing itself entails knowledge of attributes and consequences both collectively and severally; no multiple independently knowing divine essences are introduced.
Comprehensive non-detailed order in divine knowledge retained, explicitly rejecting the Peripatetic causal argument for separately existent effects.
Quiddities/known entities qua not other are intelligible; qua distinct they are not separately actual here, with both receptive and efficient forms of presence rejected in the specified context.
الوجودين غير الفرضيين is retained as non-suppositional modes with a distinct printed العرضي alternative in the commentary; no categorical emendation.
Correlative knowing/known objection and self-knowledge counterexample are stated, with the first reply explicitly dialectical.
Difference of quiddities is conceptual/relational under genuine unity, and no externally independent instance follows in this register.
Self-presence qua identical with absolute identity is distinguished from being other.
Emergence from unseen to witnessing and actuality of differentiated determinations are maintained as claims about manifestation, not as an extra self-subsisting essence.
Successive worlds of spirits, imaginal and bodies correctly ordered, while first heavenly body and cosmic Throne reflect the source's own cosmology.
The cosmic Throne as bodily terminus and ordering of world-level ranks preserved; attribution remains medieval, not modern physics.
The author refers details of proofs to separate philosophical works without importing those other books' contents.
The six-part objection begins with modality/necessity and denial that quiddities and relations are made, as an opponent's claim.
Second objection attacks manifestation and any reification of either a whole or its components, including mental and external being.
Objection further denies possible differences between world of meanings and world of witnessing.
Objection alleges names/essences differ only relative to subjects and disallows summary/detail distinction.
Imaginal world is denied by the reported Peripatetic opponents, not by the author's ultimate doctrine.
Final horn rejects greater manifestation at lowest level and argues higher unchanging levels would be more complete; the response follows in QT-035.
Reply makes determinations the subject of possibility, while allowing incidental existence to quiddities, relations and name-aspects.
Existing quiddities can be produced because their being-existent comes through conjunction with existence which is other than quiddity.
Being existent by accident versus self-subsisting being, and derivative conceptual existential predication, are kept distinct.
Conclusion warns against confusing intellectual predication of existence with the underlying reality of unrestricted existence.
The printed original repeats an assertion about less-than-complete external forms. English acknowledges the repeated statement instead of disguising it as new substantive content.
Higher and immediately lower manifestations are distinct; the two-world comparison is rhetorical, not independently established.
Author cites a separate al-Ḥikma al-Manīʿa for expanded argument without inserting external content.
Charitable 'perhaps they meant' interpretation of greater perfection at final sensory level preserved rather than unconditional superiority.
Higher completeness as comprehensiveness of cognitive modes and activity preserved.
Concluding exhortation retained.
Acquired malakāt and sensory apprehension as non-obstructive of the soul's other forms of cognition preserved.
Death as completion and preservation of perfected soul's capacities is the text's metaphysical assertion, not contemporary empirical evidence.
Longer proof explicitly deferred by author.
From predominance of unity through dispersed multiplicity to will for a comprehensive locus is a single complex conditional movement, not three disconnected beings.
Comprehensive locus gathers luminous/shadow, hidden/open, inward/outward without equating the Real with a physical aggregate.
Perfect Human as encompassing appearance of the essence and divine names, attributes and acts retained.
Necessary/possible and unity/differentiation as relationally gathered human correspondences preserved.
The divine self-apprehension claim remains attributed to the author and grounded in the comprehensive manifestation.
The embedded mirror quotation (closely related to Fuṣūṣ) is explicitly examined critically; nested quotation not attributed as the ancestor's original formulation.
Intellectual vision contrasted with sensory sight and First Intellect as possible mirror.
Sensory object as corporeal accident versus derivative sight of matter underlines the argument, without mistaking it for modern scientific observation.
Objection claims only comprehensive Perfect Human preserves all divine names and forms, not the First Intellect.
Reply denies that the whole identity is directly apprehended in every level; some forms remain intellectually unseen.
Three alternatives—identity with human, unrestricted being, or composite of determinations—are distinguished.
Macrocosm analogy to a human formal whole treated as proposed hypothesis, not proved natural unity.
Temporal heterogeneity of cosmic species and innumerable perfections prevent any one embodied individual from exhausting the universal image.
Seal of Prophets and Seal of Saints perfections are discussed as the author's dialectical constraints.
Dilemma: if perfected self-knowledge not a perfection, it cannot be final cause; if real perfection, dependence follows.
Dependence on a contingent originated composite would negate necessity in every respect.
Reply to being 'other' clarifies dependence precisely on receptive plurality and conjunction.
Objection: stripping restraints and suspending bodily faculties appears incompatible with comprehensive manifestation.
The opponents' description of ascetic training and cognitive faculties is accurately framed as reported argument.
Absent analogues to rebellious spirits and beasts listed as an objection, not an endorsement of their literal absence.
Celestial spheres' supposed incorruptibility is source's inherited cosmology, explicitly labelled as such.
Objection to suprarational perfection treats its alleged ineffability and unavailability to bodily powers as a difficulty for the opponents.
Death versus voluntary attention as proposed condition for complete detachment distinguished.
Natural limitations allegedly remaining even after death are included, not suppressed.
Humoral counter-accusation is analogical/dialectical, not endorsed as medical diagnosis or universal criticism of Sufi practice.
Excessive hunger and sleeplessness rendered accurately for السهر here, unlike corrected SH-058 السهو.
Weakening of constitution and supposed cognitive defects are presented as opponent's claims.
Four degrees of comprehensiveness and differentiated knowledge presented in sequence.
Reply to 'only intellectual' explicitly cites all levels, including complete self-apprehension and source-page interleaved Persian marginalia excluded.
Intellectual, estimative, imaginative and sensory modes gathered together with corresponding receptivities.
Form of whole characterized through active determinations and human receptivities.
The one فلئن قيل objection has two branches; an earlier English translation incorrectly introduced 'we reply' before the second branch. Both horns now precede قلنا.
The sole قلنا is the beginning of reply, which contrasts divine necessary aspects from possible created aspects, not a second objection.
One unrestricted reality under hidden/manifest/locus relations, while not identical under differing conceptual predications.
Balanced elemental body and faculties are interpreted through the author's philosophical physiology.
A naturally one body–soul substance distinguished from bare plurality of principles.
The cosmos can have aggregative unity, not natural species-unity in this argument; the proofs are deferred.

issues: Three passages corrected; one passage contains two connected technical-semantic corrections; additional textual cruxes flagged without conjectural emendation.
